 FLINT, Mich. – The City of Flint is implementing a new system with the Michigan Department of Treasury that is set to help residents file and pay their city income tax.
 Flint Mayor Sheldon Neeley and Chief Deputy State Treasurer Lance Wilkinson held a press conference on Thursday to discuss the new system.
 The new state administered system will allow residents to electronically file their Flint tax return along with their state individual income tax return beginning in 2027.
 Organizers say the new system will benefit residents by:
 Enabling online services for taxpayers to electronically file, pay, and self-manage their accounts
 Providing faster refunds and improve accuracy with built-in validations
 Allowing for centralized support with multichannel communications, such as messaging, phone and email
 Currently, the City of Flint's Income Tax Division oversees the collection and enforcement of the city's income tax.
 City of Flint taxes include a 1% tax rate for residents and a 0.5% tax rate for non-residents working within the city.
